title: Mass-imbalanced SU(N) Fermi gases
authors: Jordi Pera, Joaquim Casulleras, Jordi Boronat
abstract: We report a fully analytical description of zero-temperature itinerant ferromagnetism in repulsive SU(N) Fermi gases with arbitrary mass imbalance among components. Using perturbation theory in the gas parameter x = kFa0, with kF the Fermi momentum and a0 the s-wave scattering length, we derive the second-order energy for arbitrary spin polarization and arbitrary mass ratio. Our main result is a closed analytic expression for the beyond-mean-field correction in mixtures with unequal masses. This analytical result extends the theory of dilute Fermi gases beyond the mass-balanced case and provides a compact equation of state for multicomponent mixtures. We show that mass imbalance breaks the paramagnetic symmetry already in the non-interacting limit, favors the occu pation of heavier components, and lowers the interaction strength required to reach a fully polarized state. For S = 1/2, the system evolves continuously from a mass-induced partially polarized state to full ferromagnetism. For larger spins, distinct mass distributions generate qualitatively differ ent polarization paths, including smooth and discontinuous sequences. Our results identify mass imbalance as a powerful control tool for magnetic ordering in ultracold Fermi mixtures.
summary: This paper analytically describes itinerant ferromagnetism in multi-component Fermi gases where the components have unequal masses. By using second-order perturbation theory, the authors show that mass imbalance fundamentally changes the magnetic transition pathway, leading to continuous polarization and requiring weaker interactions than previously thought. This highlights mass mismatch as a key control parameter for quantum magnetism.
main_problem: The study focuses on deriving a fully analytical description of zero-temperature itinerant ferromagnetism in repulsive SU(N) Fermi gases that possess arbitrary mass imbalance among their components.
main_result: Mass imbalance fundamentally alters the magnetic ordering path, causing the system to approach full polarization continuously rather than discontinuously, and it lowers the interaction strength required for ferromagnetism.
method: The authors employ perturbation theory up to second order in the gas parameter x = kF a0 to derive closed analytical expressions for the beyond-mean-field energy corrections.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a repulsive SU(N) Fermi gas at zero temperature, characterized by multiple spin components and varying mass ratios among these components. The interactions are governed by an s-wave scattering length $a_0$.
key_observables: Energy per particle (E/N), polarization (P), occupation factors ($C_\lambda$), and the critical gas parameter required for full polarization.
important_parameters: The mass imbalance is quantified by ratios like $r_\lambda = m_g / m_\lambda$, and the coupling strength is controlled by the gas parameter $x$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbation theory truncated at the second order in the gas parameter x.
figures_summary: Figures compare energy vs. interaction strength for mass-balanced versus mass-imbalanced systems, and plot the critical gas parameter needed to reach full polarization as a function of the maximum mass ratio.
paper_structure: The paper develops the analytical second-order energy expression for arbitrary mass ratios, analyzes how mass imbalance breaks paramagnetic symmetry even at weak coupling, and demonstrates that this asymmetry modifies the entire path toward magnetic ordering compared to the mass-balanced case.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool showing how external parameters like mass mismatch can act as a control knob for inducing or modifying quantum phase transitions (like ferromagnetism) in ultracold atomic mixtures.
